correctness.rationale: For s>=1, nonzero H2 forces a composable two-arrow chain on three objects. The trisp has f=(3,a+b+c,ab) and Euler identity c=(a-1)(b-1)-s+1, giving the universal lower bound. The anchor row/column construction exists for every uv>=s, kills pi1 and has free H2 of rank s; homological Whitehead yields the claimed wedge. Exact finite optimization follows by taking v=ceil(s/u). The included checker verifies boundary identities and maximal ranks on 400 finite constructions; it is supporting, not universal proof.

value.rationale: The source establishes a sharp count of objects but notes a tradeoff in morphisms; the sharp count of nonidentity arrows at the object-minimal three objects is a natural finer resource measure. The theorem gives a complete arithmetic classification for all positive sphere multiplicities, constructively improves the linear family s+4 to square-root order, and reveals nonmonotonic costs (mu_3(7)=10, mu_3(8)=9). It is not implied by object minimality or a single finite census.
